visit_note.text:
Date of visit: 2026-03-23
Patient: 76-year-old woman, established patient.
Chief complaint: worsening leg weakness with low back pain
History: low back pain for a week; foot drop developing over the last 48 hours.
Examination: ankle dorsiflexion 2/5, clearly weaker than two days ago.
Assessment: progressive motor deficit, lumbar nerve root compression suspected.
Plan: MRI of the lumbar spine this afternoon. Because the weakness is progressing, imaging could not be delayed.
Electronically signed by the treating clinician, 2026-03-23.

supporting_documents.text:
Billing note, 2026-04-16
Claim submitted 2026-03-26.
Authorization request for the urgent service sent 2026-04-02, with the clinic note.
The plan declined to accept the request because a claim was already on file.

expected.rationale: One clause allows a request within 14 days of an urgent service, and this one was made in time. Another refuses any request once a claim is on file, and the claim went in first. The policies do not say which prevails, so a person decides.
